Updated assessment using SLOOS: While the FOMC statement notes solid job gains, low unemployment, and moderate growth with below-target inflation—supporting a dovish hold and continued ample-reserves operations—the SLOOS points to tightening credit conditions that temper this optimism. Banks reported tighter standards and terms for C&I and construction/land development loans, higher credit score thresholds and tighter credit limits, weaker demand in consumer and construction loans, and expectations for 2020 of further tightening, reduced risk tolerance, and some deterioration in loan performance/collateral values. Although some categories show unchanged or slightly stronger consumer loan demand, the net SLOOS signal is a tighter bank-lending channel and softer demand, which are headwinds for business investment and parts of household spending. Net tone shifts from slightly positive to guarded/slightly positive.
